transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 10:15 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Romero (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood Solutions), Priya Kapoor (NimbusGrid Head of Platform), Tomás Alvarez (NimbusGrid CTO), Ethan Lo (NimbusGrid SRE), Sara Menon (NimbusGrid Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood ran through marketplace listing requirements, packaging expectations (Helm + container image layout), and the VPC connector auth flow. Main blockers: KMS key policy shape for cross-account encryption, egress rules for their on-prem connector, and a request for a preflight runbook. Agreed next steps include sharing checklist, preparing UAT staging, and scheduling a follow-up demo.

Topics: packaging checklist, VPC connector handshake, KMS/HSM compatibility, on-prem networking, quantized model variants fallback

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Uh, I see Priya, Tomás, Ethan, Sara, thanks for making time.
[00:00:18] Priya Kapoor: Hey Maya, thanks. Quick note we only have 62 minutes, so we'll try to keep the intros short.
[00:00:28] Alex Romero: Great, we'll do a focused agenda — packaging checklist, VPC connector flow, KMS notes, and then Q&A / next steps.
[00:00:45] Tomás Alvarez: Sounds good. We're mostly here to make sure the marketplace listing won't hit any blockers for our SecOps team, and to confirm the network and KMS bits.
[00:00:58] Maya Chen: Exactly. Jordan and I will own packaging and listing, Alex will deep-dive into the connector and the auth flow.
[00:01:12] Jordan Patel: Quick context: NimbusGrid wants a joint solution listing with a hybrid connector so customers can run inference on-prem or in their VPC and still get the Redwood runtime managed updates.
[00:01:30] Sara Menon: Security priority for us: KMS integration must support key rotation and we need audit log details. Also, we want to know if Redwood can support customer-managed HSMs.
[00:01:46] Alex Romero: Short answer: we do support KMS integrations and HSMs in principle, though HSM onprem can be tricky — we'll share the compatibility matrix.
[00:01:58] Ethan Lo: When you say "support" is that out of the box or needs extra work from Redwood? We have strict egress policies so any connector needs to fit that flow.
[00:02:12] Alex Romero: Good point. The connector has two flavors: hosted-control-plane with VPC peering, or private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed. For marketplace listing we're typically packaging the hosted-controller connector with a Helm chart that customers install into their cluster; it opens a small set of outbound ports to Redwood control plane endpoints.
[00:02:36] Priya Kapoor: We prefer the VPC peering model for our enterprise customers, but our security folks want to avoid open internet egress. Can the connector work with only private endpoints?
[00:02:51] Alex Romero: Yes, you can provision private endpoints and we have a VPC connector mode. There was, uh, one caveat — for model downloads and container images we rely on a pull-from-registry pattern; if you want fully air-gapped, we can provide an on-prem bundle, but that's extra packaging.
[00:03:12] Tomás Alvarez: Okay that clarifies. Next, KMS: Sara, do you have a preferred KMS vendor?
[00:03:22] Sara Menon: We use a mix — AWS KMS in cloud tenants, and HashiCorp Vault on prem. We need to know what policies and roles Redwood expects for cross-account decrypt.
[00:03:36] Alex Romero: We'll send the KMS policy template. For cross-account decrypt we usually ask for an IAM role with a condition that limits decryption to the Redwood service principal — it'll be in the doc. For Vault, we have a short guide; you can either mount a token or use mTLS to the Vault CA.
[00:03:56] Maya Chen: Note, I'll attach the KMS template to the follow-up. Also we'll include a gap doc for HSM compatibility.
[00:04:08] Priya Kapoor: Great. On packaging: what does the marketplace expect? Single OCI image? Helm plus values?
[00:04:18] Jordan Patel: Our standard is a Helm chart that references OCI images. We also require a quickstart that shows minimum RBAC and network policies. For the listing page, a short reference architecture diagram and an example values.yaml are typical.
[00:04:36] Tomás Alvarez: Do you have sample charts we can reuse?
[00:04:40] Jordan Patel: Yes, we'll share a sample Helm chart in the repo. We'll also provide a packaging checklist — things like provenance, SBOM, image signing notes, and runtime constraints.
[00:04:52] Ethan Lo: SBOM and signing are musts for our legal team. Also, how do you handle runtime model variants — like quantized models for low-latency instances — will those be separate images or runtime flags?
[00:05:08] Alex Romero: We generally surface model variants as different model artifacts managed in the Redwood catalog. Runtime can swap to a quantized variant on fallback. For the connector we ship the model artifact reference; downloading happens at runtime. If you want pre-pulled models on-prem, we can include a sidecar syncer in the chart.
[00:05:31] Priya Kapoor: Would pre-pulling models solve our egress concerns?
[00:05:35] Alex Romero: Yes, pre-pulling avoids outbound image/model pulls during runtime. You'd want to orchestrate the sync from a controlled registry inside your network.
[00:05:46] Tomás Alvarez: On observability: what telemetry flows do we need to forward to Redwood? Any personal data or are tokens scrubbed?
[00:05:56] Maya Chen: By default we scrub PII and we provide token-level cost and latency traces only if customer opts in. For the marketplace listing we usually keep telemetry optional — minimal traces for health checks are recommended.
[00:06:12] Sara Menon: Audit logs question: do you expose raw request logs or only metadata? Our compliance requires full audit trails for decrypt events.
[00:06:22] Alex Romero: We can provide audit logs for control plane actions — model deployments, key rotation events, successful/failed decrypt ops. Raw request payloads are not stored unless configured; there are compliance add-ons for extended retention.
[00:06:39] Priya Kapoor: Let's talk about the actual listing process — what's the gating?
[00:06:45] Jordan Patel: Gating is: packaging checklist completion, security review (SBOM, signing), KMS/HSM compatibility check, and UAT with connector deployed in a staging environment. After that we do a marketplace validation run and publishing. Typical lead time ~3-4 weeks if nothing blocks.
[00:07:03] Tomás Alvarez: 3-4 weeks for a first-pass publish — good to know. For UAT, can Redwood host a preflight script or do we run it ourselves?
[00:07:14] Alex Romero: We provide a preflight script (shell/helm-based) that verifies RBAC, network connectivity, and KMS handshake. We can run it with you or you can run and share results.
[00:07:28] Ethan Lo: We'll likely run it ourselves and invite Redwood to review the logs.
[00:07:32] Maya Chen: Perfect — action item: we'll send the preflight and checklist.
[00:07:40] Priya Kapoor: One more: licensing and billing metadata. How does the listing surface pricing? Is it pay-as-you-go via Redwood or via NimbusGrid?
[00:07:51] Jordan Patel: Two options: Redwood-billed hosted usage or marketplace listing with a pass-through metering integrator. For enterprise customers we recommend marketplace listing that directs to a contract between Redwood and NimbusGrid — we can include metering hooks if you want metering to attribute usage back to NimbusGrid.
[00:08:12] Tomás Alvarez: We'll probably want metering attribution so NimbusGrid can reconcile usage. What's required for that?
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: You'll need an account mapping and a webhook endpoint to receive billing events — we'll include the spec.
[00:08:29] Sara Menon: Back to network: you mentioned private endpoints earlier; will the VPC connector require cross-account peering or do you rely on AWS PrivateLink?
[00:08:38] Alex Romero: We prefer PrivateLink where available; peering is possible but adds more ops. PrivateLink gives you private IPs and avoids route table complexity.
[00:08:50] Priya Kapoor: Good. For regions: we need EU and APAC availability. Do you have region-specific images or is it centralized?
[00:08:59] Jordan Patel: Images are replicated to registries in each major region; control plane has regional endpoints. For the listing, we document region support per offering.
[00:09:10] Tomás Alvarez: Okay. Now can we do a quick walkthrough of the connector handshake?
[00:09:14] Alex Romero: Sure — I'll share my screen for a 6-minute deep dive. (brief pause)
[00:09:30] [screen share start — light audio noise]
[00:09:33] Alex Romero: Step one: install our Helm chart which creates a connector pod and an agent. The agent does an initial mTLS handshake with Redwood's control plane, establishing a signed cert. It then registers the cluster with the customer org id.
[00:09:55] Ethan Lo: mTLS — do we need our own certificates or does the agent request via ACME?
[00:10:02] Alex Romero: Agent can request certs from a local CA if you have one, or it can use the built-in CSR flow to Redwood which returns a cert signed by our intermediate CA. If you need mutual auth to your Vault, that's supported.
[00:10:15] Priya Kapoor: That CSR flow — would that require outbound call to Redwood? If we're trying to avoid internet egress that's a blocker.
[00:10:25] Alex Romero: If you want zero egress, you can use a pre-baked cert or a PKI issued by your CA — the chart supports mounting certs. The CSR flow is convenience for hosted deployments.
[00:10:39] Tomás Alvarez: For KMS decrypt calls, is the decrypt performed locally or proxied?
[00:10:45] Alex Romero: Decrypt happens where the keys live. If keys are in customer KMS, the connector will call the KMS local endpoint. If keys are in Redwood-managed KMS, we proxy decrypt events but never store plaintext; we keep audit events.
[00:10:59] Sara Menon: Proxying decrypt across accounts will need careful IAM scoping. We'll review the policy template.
[00:11:07] Alex Romero: Agreed. We'll send that. Also, if you want HSM attestation, we can require attestation before any key usage. That typically needs a custom add-on.
[00:11:20] Priya Kapoor: Good nuance. Any gotchas for Helm values we should be aware of?
[00:11:25] Jordan Patel: Watch out for clusterRole and clusterRoleBinding since some clusters block wide RBAC. We have a namespaced install for limited-permission installs. Also, the sidecar syncer requires a PersistentVolumeClaim if you pre-pull models.
[00:11:42] Ethan Lo: We'll probably use namespaced install. For PVC sizing, what's the guideline per model size?
[00:11:48] Alex Romero: Depends on model— a 2B model ~ 8-12GB post-quantization, larger models accordingly. We'll include a sizing guide.
[00:11:58] Tomás Alvarez: Let's call out quantization: do you support INT8 and FP16 variants? How are those surfaced?
[00:12:06] Alex Romero: We support FP16 on GPUs and INT8 for certain kernels — the runtime auto-selects kernels based on hardware. Quantized artifacts are separate model files in the catalog.
[00:12:18] Priya Kapoor: That works. One concern — fallback behavior: if quantized fails at runtime, will the request fail or fall back to a different variant?
[00:12:27] Alex Romero: We have an automatic fallback policy: if a quantized kernel fails, we can route to a CPU-hosted variant or a larger GPU variant. That routing is configurable in the connector policy.
[00:12:38] Priya Kapoor: Excellent.
[00:12:41] [00:12:41 — small cross talk, someone drops audio briefly]
[00:12:55] Maya Chen: Quick pause — any blocking security items we haven't addressed?
[00:13:02] Sara Menon: KMS policy template and HSM compatibility matrix are the biggest open asks. Also need the SBOM and image signing details.
[00:13:12] Jordan Patel: We'll attach SBOM generation instructions and image signing CI examples.
[00:13:19] Tomás Alvarez: For the UAT, what metrics should we capture? Latency, token rate, and concurrency?
[00:13:27] Alex Romero: Yes capture p99 latency, token/sec, and error rate per model. Also trace cache hit rates since KV/prefix caching can significantly change p99s.
[00:13:41] Ethan Lo: On KV cache — does the connector support remote KV cache across shards? We have multi-cluster workloads.
[00:13:48] Alex Romero: We support local KV cache and a remote cache layer for cross-cluster sharing; remote cache uses a Redis or memcached backend — we have docs.
[00:14:00] Priya Kapoor: Great. A few administrative items: for the listing imagery and blurb, who from Redwood owns the final copy?
[00:14:07] Maya Chen: I'll own the copy. Jordan will review the architecture diagram. We'll send a draft to Priya by 2026-05-03.
[00:14:16] Priya Kapoor: Thanks.
[00:14:20] [00:14:20 — 30 second pause while Maya pastes links in chat]
[00:14:50] Maya Chen: Shared: marketplace packaging checklist link (https://redwood.example/marketplace-packaging), sample Helm repo (https://git.redwood.example/nimbusgrid-sample-chart), KMS policy template (https://redwood.example/kms-template).
[00:15:02] Priya Kapoor: Got them. We'll review and follow up with specific comments.
[00:15:08] Tomás Alvarez: One final technical ask — can we get a short perf baseline for your inference runtime on 1xA100 and 2xA100 setups so we can size our GPU fleet?
[00:15:20] Alex Romero: Yes, we have perf profiles — I'll attach the perf matrix. Note that quantization and batch sizes change throughput a lot; we'll include a couple of sample runs.
[00:15:34] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. Anything else from Redwood?
[00:15:37] Maya Chen: No, just to reiterate next steps. We'll (1) share checklist and Helm repo (2) Alex shares KMS policy + perf matrix (3) NimbusGrid shares network diagram and picks UAT week.
[00:15:51] Priya Kapoor: We aim to have docs ready by May 7th and schedule UAT week of May 11th.
[00:15:59] Maya Chen: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[00:16:05] [End of main discussion. Remaining time used to clarify Slack channels and doc links, brief side conversations; transcript below samples some of that chatter, recognitions are imperfect]
[00:16:20] Tomás Alvarez: small note — the repo path had a typo earlier, might be "nimbusgrid-sample-chart" — we'll check.
[00:16:30] Jordan Patel: Yep, fixed in chat.
[00:16:40] Ethan Lo: Also we'll include a compliance contact for legal questions.
[00:16:45] Sara Menon: Thanks.
[00:16:50] Maya Chen: Awesome. Thanks everyone. Talk soon.
[00:17:00] [call wrap, soft chatter until end — meeting ends at ~10:17:10 PDT]

- Will the connector support fully air-gapped installs? (Answer: yes, with on-prem bundle and pre-pulled models, but requires extra packaging)

- Is image signing and SBOM required for listing? (Answer: yes, recommended; will share generation steps)
